answer: An agent market requires each seller to lock a refundable bond before accepting jobs, whether selling sparrow population counts, ember detection data, or ferrous scrap assessments. The bond stays locked through a dispute window and is forfeited if a seller submits provably fabricated results. Creating identities is cheap, but operating 1,000 sellers requires 1,000 bonds, tying up the attacker’s capital and exposing it to loss when fraud is proved.
